## What is IrisPipe?

IrisPipe is a **single-user pipeline engine console** that lets you define, execute,
and monitor multi-stage data pipelines against arbitrary JDBC sources and destinations.

It is intentionally scoped for **local / desktop use** — no cloud dependency, no agent,
no daemon. You define a pipeline, press Execute, and observe it run step-by-step with
real-time SSE event push.

## Pipeline Structure

Every pipeline is a directed acyclic sequence of stages.
Stages run sequentially; jobs within a stage run in parallel.

::: {.concept-node}Pipeline
:::

::: {.concept-node}Stage 1
:::
::: {.concept-arrow}→
:::
::: {.concept-node}Stage 2
:::
::: {.concept-arrow}→
:::
::: {.concept-node}Stage N
:::
:::

## Three Execution Verbs

The key differentiator in IrisPipe's design is how it models **re-execution**:

| Verb | Creates | Reads config from | Starts at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `execute` | New logical run | Live stored config | Stage 1 |
| `resume` | New attempt in existing run | Frozen snapshot | First incomplete stage |
| `rerun` | New logical run | Frozen snapshot | Stage 1 |

`resume` and `rerun` both operate on a **config snapshot** taken at execute time —
so a pipeline can be modified without corrupting in-flight or historical runs.
